gaps.explanation: Statement lines come from the accrual proprietary funds statement p6 (printed p8): total operating revenues 540,523 + interest and investment revenue 3,243 = 543,766 (Water 319,308 + 1,506 = 320,814; Sewer 221,215 + 1,737 = 222,952; Other Proprietary Fund 0). Detail comes from the budgetary-basis schedules: Water p17 (printed p29) total revenues 329,861, Sewer p18 (p30) 217,754, Meter Deposit Fund p19 (p31) Miscellaneous 2,700 = 550,315. Per fund: Water 329,861 - 320,814 = 9,047; Sewer 217,754 - 222,952 = -5,198; Meter Deposit 2,700 => 6,549 = schedule excess. Both totals correct on their own basis; no fix.

Accrual statement p6: total operating expenses 719,791 (incl. depreciation 125,138) + interest expense 353 = 720,144 (Water 390,807; Sewer 328,984 + 353 = 329,337). Budgetary schedules: Water p17 total expenditures 311,163 (no depreciation), Sewer p18 326,304 (incl. debt service 19,833, capital outlay 28,510), Meter Deposit p19 1,800 = 639,267. Per fund: Water 311,163 - 390,807 = -79,644; Sewer 326,304 - 329,337 = -3,033; Meter Deposit +1,800 => -80,877, i.e. the schedule is 80,877 short = gap. Depreciation (accrual only) vs capital outlay/debt principal (budgetary only); no line missing; no fix.
